questions.question: The path followed by a projectile is called its:
questions.explanation: The path traced by a projectile is its trajectory. An orbit is a closed path under a central force; displacement and angular displacement are different quantities.

questions.question: At the highest point of a projectile's path, its vertical velocity is:
questions.explanation: At the highest point the projectile stops rising, so its vertical velocity is zero. The horizontal velocity is unchanged.

questions.question: The trajectory of a projectile, with air resistance neglected, is:
options: an ellipse centered on the launch point
questions.explanation: Eliminating t between x = uxt and y = uyt − ½gt² gives y = ax − bx², a parabola.

questions.question: The maximum horizontal range for a projectile on level ground occurs at a projection angle of:
options: 90° above the horizontal, which gives the greatest range
questions.explanation: Range R = (u² sin 2θ) ÷ g is maximum when sin 2θ = 1, i.e. 2θ = 90°, so θ = 45°. At 90° the projectile rises vertically and has zero range.

questions.question: In projectile motion, gravity affects:
options: both components equally at all times
neither component once the projectile has left the launcher
questions.explanation: Gravity acts vertically, so it affects only the vertical velocity; the horizontal velocity is unaffected when air resistance is neglected.

questions.question: A football kicked across a field is an example of:
options: motion with zero acceleration at every instant
questions.explanation: After being kicked, the ball moves under gravity along a parabolic path — projectile motion.

questions.question: A stone tied to a string and whirled at constant speed undergoes:
options: motion with no acceleration because its speed is constant
questions.explanation: The stone moves along a circle at constant speed, so it undergoes uniform circular motion. Its speed is constant but its velocity changes direction, so D is false.

questions.question: In uniform circular motion, the speed is:
questions.explanation: Uniform circular motion means the speed is constant; only the direction of velocity changes.

questions.question: In uniform circular motion, the velocity vector:
options: remains constant in both magnitude and direction
is always directed away from the centre
has a magnitude that decreases toward the centre of the circle
questions.explanation: The velocity is always tangent to the circle, so its direction changes continuously while its magnitude (speed) stays constant.

questions.question: The acceleration directed toward the centre of a circular path is called:
options: tangential acceleration caused by a change in speed along the path
questions.explanation: The inward acceleration responsible for changing the direction of velocity is the centripetal acceleration, a = v² ÷ r, directed toward the centre.

questions.question: For a stone whirled on a string, the string exerts on the stone a force directed:
options: opposite to the stone's weight only
questions.explanation: The tension in the string pulls the stone inward toward the centre, providing the centripetal force.

questions.question: Centrifugal force is best described as:
options: a real force pushing objects outward from every circle
a fictitious force appearing in a rotating frame
the same as centripetal force but opposite in direction
a force that acts only when the speed of the object is changing
questions.explanation: Centrifugal force is a fictitious (pseudo) force introduced by an observer in a rotating, non-inertial frame. It is not a real interaction force.

questions.question: Angular speed is defined as:
options: linear distance covered per unit time
change in speed per unit time
questions.explanation: Angular speed ω is the angle swept per unit time: ω = Δθ ÷ Δt. B is linear speed, C is tangential acceleration.

questions.question: The SI unit of angular speed is:
questions.explanation: Angular speed is angle per time, so its SI unit is rad/s.

questions.question: The relation between linear speed and angular speed for circular motion is:
questions.explanation: Linear speed equals angular speed times radius: v = ωr. B and C are dimensionally wrong; D is the centripetal acceleration.

questions.question: Angular displacement is related to arc length by:
questions.explanation: For a circle, arc length = radius × angular displacement (in radians): s = rθ.

questions.question: The period of revolution is the:
options: number of revolutions per unit time
questions.explanation: The period T is the time for one complete revolution. A is angular speed, C is circumference, D is frequency.

questions.question: If the string holding a whirling stone cuts, the stone will move off with:
options: a velocity directed outward along the string
questions.explanation: When the string cuts, the inward force disappears. By inertia the stone continues with the velocity it had at that instant, which is tangential to the circle.

questions.question: The Earth revolving around the Sun is an example of:
questions.explanation: The Earth moves around the Sun under gravitational attraction, executing (approximately) circular motion with a centripetal acceleration toward the Sun.

questions.question: The vertical velocity of a projectile decreases as it rises because:
options: air resistance pushes it downward only
questions.explanation: Gravity acts downward, opposite to the upward motion, so the vertical velocity decreases by g each second.

questions.question: The horizontal velocity of a projectile remains constant because:
options: the launch angle is always exactly 45°, which removes all horizontal forces
questions.explanation: Gravity has no horizontal component, so with air resistance neglected there is no horizontal force and the horizontal velocity is constant.

questions.question: The maximum height of a projectile depends on:
options: mass and colour of the projectile
the radius of the Earth and the mass of the projectile together
questions.explanation: Maximum height H = uy² ÷ (2g) depends only on the initial vertical velocity component and g.

questions.question: A projectile launched horizontally has an initial vertical velocity component of:
questions.explanation: A horizontal launch has no initial vertical velocity, so uy = 0. Its initial velocity is entirely horizontal.

questions.question: The centripetal force on an object in circular motion is directed:
options: along the tangent to the path
toward the centre of the circle
away from the centre of the circle
questions.explanation: Centripetal force is always directed toward the centre of the circular path. A is the direction of velocity; C is centrifugal; D is not generally true.

questions.question: The angular speed of a body making one complete revolution in time T is:
questions.explanation: One revolution corresponds to an angle of 2π radians in time T, so ω = 2π ÷ T. B is the reciprocal, C and D are dimensionally wrong.
